```yaml
    handle: community

    label: Load Groups

      maxTokens: 200

      kind: scheduled

      group_counts: "{{ count_by_groupTypes.output }}"
```

```yaml
descriptor:
  id: top-noncompliant-models
  name: Top Noncompliant Models
  description: Lists the oldest managed devices by model and compliance state.
  version: 0.1.0
  minAppVersion: 0.1.0
  author:
    name: Community
    handle: community
  category: devices
  mode: read
  preferredModel: gpt-4o-mini
skills:
  - id: load_devices
    format: graph
    label: Load managed devices
    detail: Retrieves managed devices with compliance and sync information.
    settings:
      method: GET
      path: /deviceManagement/managedDevices
      select:
        - id
        - deviceName
        - model
        - complianceState
        - lastSyncDateTime
      scopes:
        - DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All
  - id: count_by_compliance
    format: transform
    label: Count devices by compliance state
    detail: Tallies devices per compliance state using predefined buckets.
    settings:
      kind: count-by-field
      source: "{{ load_devices.output }}"
      field: complianceState
      buckets:
        - compliant
        - noncompliant
        - unknown
  - id: sort_by_last_sync
    format: transform
    label: Sort devices by last sync
    detail: Orders devices by lastSyncDateTime ascending and keeps the oldest 10.
    settings:
      kind: sort-by
      source: "{{ load_devices.output }}"
      field: lastSyncDateTime
      direction: asc
      take: 10
  - id: summarize
    format: llm
    label: Summarize results
    detail: Generates a concise report of the oldest noncompliant devices.
    settings:
      system: You are a Microsoft 365 admin assistant. Provide clear, actionable summaries.
      prompt: >-
        Here are the oldest managed devices (up to 10) with their model and compliance state:
        {{ sort_by_last_sync.output }}

        Summarize the findings, highlighting any noncompliant devices and their models.
      temperature: 0.2
      maxTokens: 200
definition:
  triggers:
    - id: manual
      kind: manual
  result:
    summary: "{{ summarize.output }}"
    data:
      total_devices: "{{ load_devices.output | length }}"
      compliance_counts: "{{ count_by_compliance.output }}"
      oldest_devices: "{{ sort_by_last_sync.output }}"
```

```yaml
slug: dormant-guest-accounts
description: Reviews guest users in the tenant and reports those that have been inactive for a configurable period.
version: 0.1.0
author: OpenAdminOS Community
icon: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openadminos/openadminos/main/assets/icons/dormant-guest-accounts.svg
category: User Management
mode: read
sources:
  - name: guest_users
    type: mgraph
    query: |
      {
        "value": [
          {
            "id": "userId",
            "displayName": "displayName",
            "userPrincipalName": "userPrincipalName",
            "userType": "userType",
            "lastSignInDateTime": "lastSignInDateTime"
          }
        ],
        "$filter": "userType eq 'Guest'"
      }
    transform: |
      [
        {
          "id": "$.value[*].id",
          "displayName": "$.value[*].displayName",
          "userPrincipalName": "$.value[*].userPrincipalName",
          "userType": "$.value[*].userType",
          "lastSignInDateTime": "$.value[*].lastSignInDateTime"
        }
      ]
steps:
  - name: summarize_dormant
    type: llm
    model: gpt-4o-mini
    prompt: |
      You are an admin assistant. The tenant has {len(guest_users)} guest users.
      Identify those that have not signed in for {dormancy_days} days or more.
      Provide a concise report: count, list of userPrincipalName, and recommendation.
    inputs:
      guest_users: "{{ guest_users }}"
      dormancy_days: 90
    outputs:
      summary: "$.text"
```
